name: cream cheese frosting
instructions:
RATIO — 2:1 CREAM CHEESE:BUTTER, THEN 1:1 TOTAL FAT:POWDERED SUGAR. Ratio still pending experiments (see notes). No milk/cream — this recipe generally doesn't need it.

1. Beat room-temp cream cheese with room-temp butter (2:1 by volume — e.g., 8 oz cream cheese : 4 oz / 1/2 cup butter) until smooth. Break up all the clumps at this stage.
2. Add 1 tsp VANILLA (LATE — see notes; vanilla is liquid, wait until clumps are gone before adding). Add a pinch of salt.
3. Gradually beat in powdered sugar at ~1:1 to total fat by weight (or ~3 cups powdered sugar for the quantities above). More sugar → stiffer.
notes:
=== RATIO — 2:1 CREAM CHEESE:BUTTER, THEN 1:1 FAT:SUGAR (PENDING EXPERIMENTS) ===

Working ratio: 2 parts cream cheese : 1 part butter (by volume), then powdered sugar equal to the total fat by weight (~1:1). Still need to run experiments to confirm this is the right landing.

Example scale: 8 oz cream cheese + 4 oz (1/2 cup) butter = 12 oz total fat → ~12 oz (~3 cups) powdered sugar.

=== REFERENCE — PREPPY KITCHEN CREAM CHEESE FROSTING ===

Captured for reference (his working recipe, not mine — helps me calibrate my ratio experiments).

INGREDIENTS:
- 3/4 cup (170g) unsalted butter, room temp
- 1 (8-oz / 226g) block cream cheese, room temp
- 1 tsp vanilla
- pinch salt
- 4 to 6 cups powdered sugar, sifted (480g-720g)

PROCEDURE (Preppy Kitchen):
1. Beat butter on medium ~30 sec until creamy.
2. Add cream cheese, vanilla, salt. Beat medium ~2 min until well combined.
3. Mixer on LOW, add powdered sugar ONE CUP AT A TIME. Mix until combined. 4 cups = softer; 6 cups = thicker.
4. Scrape down sides and bottom. Beat on medium-low ~1 min until fluffy.
5. Transfer to piping bag or spread. Yields: 2 dozen cupcakes / 1 (8-inch) 2-layer cake / 1 (13x9) sheet.

RATIO CONTRAST vs MY WORKING RATIO:
- Cream cheese : butter — Preppy Kitchen ~4:3 (226g:170g). MY WORKING ratio was 2:1. Preppy Kitchen is LESS cream-cheese-heavy than mine.
- Fat : sugar — Preppy Kitchen ~1:1.2 to 1:1.8 by weight (396g fat : 480g-720g sugar). MY WORKING ratio was 1:1. Preppy Kitchen is MORE sugar-heavy than mine.
- Net: Preppy Kitchen's frosting is more butter-forward and sweeter than mine. Something to check when running the ratio experiments.

GEL FOOD COLORING NOTE (from Preppy Kitchen): use gel (not liquid) — more concentrated color and won't thin the frosting.

=== NO MILK / CREAM NEEDED ===

This recipe generally doesn't need milk or cream — the cream cheese carries enough moisture on its own, and the finished frosting reads better without the extra liquid diluting it. Some cream cheese frosting recipes call for a splash of milk or cream to loosen the texture; skip that here.

=== VANILLA IS MORE LOAD-BEARING HERE THAN IT SEEMS IN BUTTERCREAM ===

Vanilla plays a bigger flavor role in this frosting than it does in buttercream. The finished frosting reads noticeably flatter without it. Don't skip.

TECHNIQUE — ADD VANILLA LATE (LIQUID GOES IN AFTER CLUMPS ARE GONE): vanilla is a liquid, so it goes in AFTER the cream cheese + butter are combined smoothly (clumps broken up). Adding it too early can prevent the clumps from breaking cleanly. Wait until you have something resembling a frosting from the 2:1 cream cheese:butter combo, then add the vanilla.

=== POWDERED SUGAR, NOT GRANULATED ===

The cornstarch in powdered sugar matters for texture.

=== BOTH FATS ROOM TEMP ===

Cream cheese and butter both need to be room temp. Cold cream cheese lumps; cold butter doesn't blend into it smoothly.

=== NOT SHELF-STABLE — NEEDS REFRIGERATION ===

Cream cheese frosting is NOT shelf-stable — needs to be kept cold. Not the pick for a party cake left on a table for hours. Same non-shelf-stable class as strawberry-compote.

Within the cake-topping family: bakers-frosting and buttercream-frosting are the shelf-stable picks; chocolate-ganache sits in between (more stable than cream cheese frosting but not fully stable due to its cream).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- buttercream-frosting: 2:1 sugar:butter, milk/cream to runniness. Sweeter, matte-fluffy when whipped right; slumps at room temp.
- bakers-frosting: crisco + water + cream of tartar. Shelf-stable, holds piping, more neutral flavor.
- caramel-frosting: caramelized dairy alternative.
- chocolate-ganache: chocolate + cream, looser format.
